quests.protocolRule: What could make this worse while help is arriving?
quests.crisisScene: A commuter train has hit a truck at a crossing. Passengers are climbing out of carriages, some are injured, and the truck driver is trapped. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REQUEST FIRE, MEDICAL AND POLICE RESPONSE AND HAVE RAIL TRAFFIC STOPPED
quests.actionGuidance: Rescue, medical care, and scene control are all needed, and stopping trains prevents a second collision.

quests.protocolRule: Are they safe just because they aren't hurt?
quests.crisisScene: Uninjured passengers are wandering along the tracks. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GET THEM OFF THE TRACKS AND TO A SAFE ASSEMBLY POINT
quests.actionGuidance: People on tracks are at risk from other trains and hazards. A gathering point also helps counting.

quests.protocolRule: What do crews need to find him?
quests.crisisScene: A passenger says a friend is still in the last carriage, trapped under a seat. Input rescue code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE CARRIAGE AND POSITION TO RESCUE CREWS
quests.actionGuidance: Location within the train helps rescuers reach him fastest.

quests.protocolRule: Which call could be fatal within minutes?
quests.crisisScene: All ambulances are committed to a major crash. Two new calls arrive: a woman with a suspected broken wrist and a man with sudden chest pain. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: GIVE THE NEXT AMBULANCE TO THE CHEST PAIN AND ADVISE ALTERNATIVE CARE FOR THE WRIST
quests.actionGuidance: Chest pain can be life-threatening, while a stable wrist injury can be handled another way.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: What would make her case more urgent?
quests.crisisScene: The woman with the wrist asks whether she should wait for an ambulance. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ADVISE OTHER TRANSPORT TO URGENT CARE IF POSSIBLE AND TO CALL BACK IF SHE WORSENS
quests.actionGuidance: She can get care without an ambulance, but new symptoms would change the plan.

quests.protocolRule: Who else might have a unit?
quests.crisisScene: A second chest pain call comes in and no ambulance is free. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REQUEST MUTUAL AID FROM NEIGHBORING AREAS AND KEEP THE CALLER ON THE LINE WITH GUIDANCE
quests.actionGuidance: Neighboring services can help when local units are exhausted, and the caller needs support meanwhile.

quests.protocolRule: What can carry the message when radio can't?
quests.crisisScene: During a wildfire evacuation, radio links between two fire teams fail. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SWITCH TO A BACKUP CHANNEL OR RELAY THROUGH DISPATCH AND CONFIRM POSITIONS
quests.actionGuidance: Backup channels or a relay keep teams informed of each other's location.

quests.protocolRule: How do you know the message got through?
quests.crisisScene: A team leader says the only road may be cut off by fire. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GIVE HIM THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE OR SAFE ZONE AND CONFIRM HE RECEIVED IT
quests.actionGuidance: A confirmed message prevents a team from acting on old information.

quests.protocolRule: Could both be right at different times?
quests.crisisScene: Two teams report different positions for the same fire front. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ASK EACH FOR LANDMARKS AND TIMES, THEN CONFIRM WHICH IS CURRENT
quests.actionGuidance: Timing and landmarks reveal whether they're describing different moments or places.

quests.protocolRule: Does 'under control' still apply?
quests.crisisScene: Crews say a warehouse fire is under control, then a caller reports rolling black smoke and a loud bang. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: UPDATE THE CREWS IMMEDIATELY, A BANG AND HEAVY SMOKE CHANGE THE RISK
quests.actionGuidance: New signs can mean a new hazard, and crews need to know at once.

quests.protocolRule: Who is now at risk?
quests.crisisScene: Crews report aerosol cans exploding inside the building. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: RECOMMEND PULLING PEOPLE BACK FROM THE BUILDING AND WIDENING THE CORDON
quests.actionGuidance: Exploding containers can throw shrapnel, so crews and bystanders should be pulled back.

quests.protocolRule: What does smoke do to people downwind?
quests.crisisScene: Nearby residents ask what to do about the smoke. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ADVISE STAYING INDOORS WITH WINDOWS CLOSED IF SMOKE REACHES THEM AND FOLLOW UPDATES
quests.actionGuidance: Staying indoors reduces exposure while officials assess the smoke.

quests.protocolRule: How many separate hazards are there?
quests.crisisScene: After a moderate earthquake, an apartment building has cracks, a resident smells gas, and some people are trapped on upper floors. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE STRUCTURAL DAMAGE, THE GAS SMELL, AND THE TRAPPED RESIDENTS, AND KEEP PEOPLE OUT
quests.actionGuidance: Damage, gas, and trapped people each shape the response and must all be reported.

quests.protocolRule: What falls from a damaged building?
quests.crisisScene: An aftershock shakes the area. Input safety code!
quests.optimalResponse: MOVE EVERYONE AWAY FROM THE BUILDING TO OPEN GROUND
quests.actionGuidance: Aftershocks can bring down weakened structures, so open ground is safer.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Can his need be met another way?
quests.crisisScene: A resident wants to go back in for his medication. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TELL HIM RESPONDERS CAN HELP WITH MEDICATION LATER AND HE SHOULDN'T RE-ENTER
quests.actionGuidance: His need is valid, but re-entry is too dangerous. Responders can arrange medication later.

quests.protocolRule: What causes confusion when many agencies arrive?
quests.crisisScene: At a chemical plant fire, fire, police, ambulance, and plant staff are all arriving, and roads are blocked by people evacuating. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ESTABLISH A SINGLE POINT OF COMMAND AND SHARE ROUTE INFORMATION
quests.actionGuidance: A single command point avoids conflicting orders and keeps information consistent.

quests.protocolRule: Can both aims be met?
quests.crisisScene: Police want to close the roads, but ambulances need a route in. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: KEEP A DESIGNATED CORRIDOR FOR EMERGENCY VEHICLES
quests.actionGuidance: A corridor lets police control crowds and ambulances still reach patients.

quests.protocolRule: Who knows what's inside?
quests.crisisScene: Plant staff know where the hazardous materials are stored. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: BRING THEM TO THE COMMAND POINT TO BRIEF THE FIREFIGHTERS
quests.actionGuidance: Local knowledge tells firefighters what they're dealing with.

quests.protocolRule: Which incidents threaten many lives?
quests.crisisScene: At a stadium, dozens of calls report a crush at gate 4, smoke at gate 7, a fight at gate 2, a lost child, and a medical problem. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: PRIORITIZE THE CRUSH AND SMOKE FIRST, THEN THE MEDICAL PROBLEM, THEN THE REST
quests.actionGuidance: Life-threatening events affecting many people come first.

quests.protocolRule: Are these separate incidents?
quests.crisisScene: Several callers describe the same crush from different sides. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: MERGE THEM INTO ONE INCIDENT WITH THE BEST LOCATION
quests.actionGuidance: Combining duplicate reports keeps the picture clear and saves resources.

quests.protocolRule: What should get bandwidth first?
quests.crisisScene: A security manager asks for updates every minute on every call. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GIVE UPDATES FOR LIFE-THREATENING INCIDENTS FIRST AND ROUTINE ONES LATER
quests.actionGuidance: Prioritizing updates keeps attention on the most serious events.

quests.protocolRule: What helps rescuers find people?
quests.crisisScene: A building collapses at a construction site. A colleague says some workers were under the rubble in a stairwell. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT HOW MANY AND WHERE THEY WERE LAST SEEN AND KEEP OTHERS OUT
quests.actionGuidance: Numbers and last-seen locations focus the search, and keeping others out prevents more casualties.

quests.protocolRule: How can you help crews hear?
quests.crisisScene: A foreman says he heard tapping under the debris. Input rescue code!
quests.optimalResponse: PASS THIS TO RESCUE CREWS AND ASK EVERYONE TO STAY QUIET NEAR THE SPOT
quests.actionGuidance: A sign of life directs the search, and quiet lets listening devices work.

quests.protocolRule: Who might be below?
quests.crisisScene: Heavy machinery starts moving rubble. Input safety code!
quests.optimalResponse: STOP IT UNTIL RESCUERS SAY IT'S SAFE, PEOPLE UNDERNEATH MAY BE HURT
quests.actionGuidance: Moving debris blindly can crush survivors or collapse voids.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: What do police need to intercept?
quests.crisisScene: During a jewelry-shop robbery shots are fired, one staff member is down, and the robbers flee in a car. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SEND POLICE AND AN AMBULANCE AND GIVE THE CAR DESCRIPTION AND DIRECTION
quests.actionGuidance: Medical care and pursuit are both needed, and the vehicle description is time-critical.

quests.protocolRule: How certain are you that the danger is gone?
quests.crisisScene: Staff hide in the back room while the injured man bleeds. They can't be sure the robbers are gone. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: IF YOU'RE SURE THEY'VE LEFT PRESS ON THE WOUND, OTHERWISE STAY HIDDEN
quests.actionGuidance: Treatment is urgent but not at the cost of another shooting. Certainty about safety matters.

quests.protocolRule: Is a guess helpful here?
quests.crisisScene: Police ask whether the robbers might return. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SAY WHAT YOU KNOW ABOUT WHERE THEY WENT AND THAT YOU DON'T KNOW IF THEY'LL RETURN
quests.actionGuidance: Honesty lets police plan for both possibilities.

quests.protocolRule: Which patients depend fully on power?
quests.crisisScene: A storm floods a hospital's basement. Power is out, ventilator patients are at risk, and ambulances can't reach the main entrance. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE VENTILATOR PATIENTS, THE POWER LOSS, AND THE ACCESS PROBLEM, AND ARRANGE BACKUP POWER AND EVACUATION
quests.actionGuidance: Dependent patients are time-critical. Access and power both must be solved.

quests.protocolRule: Who can't survive without equipment?
quests.crisisScene: Staff can hand-ventilate some patients but not all. Input safety code!
quests.optimalResponse: EVACUATE THE MOST DEPENDENT PATIENTS FIRST
quests.actionGuidance: Those who rely on machines are at highest risk without power.

quests.protocolRule: When was 'stable' last checked?
quests.crisisScene: A hospital official says all patients are stable. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: VERIFY WITH A CURRENT PATIENT LIST, CONDITIONS CAN CHANGE WITHOUT POWER
quests.actionGuidance: Conditions can change quickly without equipment, so status needs to be current.
